children: Sigma Advanced Systems has signed an exclusive memorandum of understanding with state-run Munitions India (MIL) to manufacture and integrate 155-mm artillery course correction fuzes in India, as the defence engineering company seeks to expand its presence in precision-guided ammunition.
The agreement covers indigenous manufacturing and supply of the fuzes, along with associated components, subsystems and technologies, Sigma said in a statement on Wednesday.

The collaboration will focus on technology transfer, qualification, localisation and integration of course correction solutions, drawing on a guidance kit currently used by international customers. The companies aim to establish domestic capabilities for advanced artillery technologies and support ongoing critical programmes of the Indian military.

Course correction technology allows artillery projectiles to adjust their trajectories during flight, potentially improving accuracy and operational effectiveness. Building domestic capabilities in the segment could help India reduce reliance on imported defence technologies.

Sigma will contribute its engineering expertise, technology and programme execution capabilities, while MIL will bring its ammunition manufacturing infrastructure and experience supplying the Indian Armed Forces.
“The collaboration with Munitions India Limited marks an important step in advancing indigenous precision-guided artillery capabilities in India,” Sigma Chief Executive Officer Sunil Kalidindi said.
The initiative is aligned with the government's Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat programmes, which seek to expand domestic defence manufacturing and reduce dependence on foreign suppliers.
For Sigma, the agreement represents an effort to move beyond precision engineering and subsystem manufacturing towards the development and integration of advanced defence systems.
MIL, one of India's largest defence public sector enterprises, manufactures ammunition and explosives and has established production facilities serving the armed forces.

The companies said the partnership would seek to progressively increase indigenous content, strengthen domestic technical expertise and build manufacturing capabilities for next-generation artillery systems.
The announcement did not disclose the financial value of the agreement, production targets or a timeline for commercial supplies.
